account: Inspection of the posterior state shows all four investigations from action:001 failed before producing any evidence (UnexpectedModelBehavior: Exceeded maximum output retries (2); zero claims, sufficiency=blocked). investigations.acceptance_condition: Complete terse proofs of L1 (1 <= d' < d at every non-root vertex), L2 (c=d only at root), L3 (mutations below the max strictly increase the max, factor >= 3), and the deductions D1, D2 (uniqueness up to sorted-vertex equality, with the equal-coordinate subtlety addressed), D3 (tree, with cycle and multiple-parent exclusion) - or an explicit verified counterexample identifying which claim fails.
investigations.independence_account: Uses only the stable definitions SC1-SC3 and elementary algebra it derives itself; needs no result from the upper/lower-bound or enumeration threads.
investigations.question: Prove D1-D3 compactly for S = {sorted quadruples 1<=a<=b<=c<=d, a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2=4abcd} under Vieta mutation (x_i -> 4*(product of others) - x_i, then re-sort), with root (1,1,1,1). REQUIRED ROUTE (verify, fix, or replace, but keep it elementary): (L1, descent) at any non-root vertex the conjugate d' = 4abc - d = (a^2+b^2+c^2)/d is an integer >= 1; prove d' < d by contradiction: d' >= d gives a^2+b^2+c^2 >= d^2, and combined with a^2+b^2+c^2 <= 3c^2 gives d <= c*sqrt(3); feeding into the equation gives 2ab <= 3, hence a=b=1; then 2+c^2+d^2 = 4cd with c <= d <= 3c/2 forces c=1 and d=1, i.e. the root - contradiction. (L2) c = d only at the root: from a^2+b^2+2d^2 = 4abd^2 deduce d^2 | a^2+b^2 and a^2+b^2 <= 2d^2, so a^2+b^2 in {d^2, 2d^2}; the first gives 3=4ab (impossible), the second gives ab=1 and then d=1. (L3) mutating any coordinate strictly below the maximum strictly increases the maximum: new value >= 4ab d - d >= 3d > d since ab >= 1 (and a=d only at root by L2-type argument). Conclude: (D2) the mutation at the unique maximal coordinate is the unique height-decreasing mutation, i.e. strictly decreases d; (D1) iterating it strictly decreases the positive integer d, so every vertex descends to d=1, and the only vertex with d=1 is (1,1,1,1) - verify this endpoint claim; (D3) the quotient graph is a rooted tree: a cycle's maximal-height vertex would have two distinct height-decreasing mutations, contradicting D2; multiple parents likewise. Address explicitly the subtlety that equal coordinates (a=b or b=c) make some of the 4 coordinate-mutations coincide after sorting, so 'unique height-decreasing mutation' is a statement about distinct mutated vertices, not coordinate indices. KEEP THE ANSWER COMPACT (target well under 1200 words): lemma - proof format, no digressions, no worked tables beyond at most 3 one-line substitution checks. If any lemma fails, stop and report the verified counterexample instead.
investigations.rationale: The previous attempt produced no evidence due to output retries; the sketched elementary route (avoiding the flawed mod-3-Pell detour in the original prompt, where m^2 = 3c^2 - 2 is NOT excludable mod 3) shortens both search and write-up. D1-D3 gate every counting argument.

investigations.acceptance_condition: Proved: child-max >= 3x parent-max off the parent edge; branching <= 3 (root: 1); N(H) <= (3H-1)/2; depth(v) <= log_3 max(v) and depth(v) >= log_3 log max(v) - O(1) with explicit constants; a clearly labeled statement of any sharper proved bound or, failing that, the precise obstruction plus a labeled conjecture. Explicit constants everywhere.
investigations.independence_account: The growth and branching lemmas are proved directly from the equation; the only external input is the tree structure, proved in parallel by struct-core-v2, and the counting argument is conditional on it in a way the synthesis can discharge.
investigations.question: From first principles, prove the strongest rigorous upper bound for N(H) = #{sorted solutions with d <= H} and the two-sided depth-vs-log-H relation, ASSUMING the tree structure (prove the per-edge growth and branching lemmas directly so the thread is self-contained where cheap). Compact plan: (i) at a non-root vertex, mutating any of the three non-maximal coordinates x gives a child with new maximum 4*(product of three others) - x >= (4ab-1)d >= 3d; hence max(v) >= 3^{depth(v)} and depth(v) <= log_3(max(v)); the root has exactly one child (1,1,1,3) - verify. (ii) Each non-root vertex has at most 3 children and the root exactly 1, so N(H) <= sum_{k=0}^{floor(log_3 H)} 3^k = (3^{floor(log_3 H)+1}-1)/2 <= (3H-1)/2 = O(H) with explicit constant. (iii) Two-sided depth relation: upper depth bound log_3 H from (i); lower bound from the coarse child estimate d_child <= 4*d^3 (since a,b,c <= d), giving log max(v) <= 3^{depth(v)} * C for an explicit constant C, hence depth(v) >= log_3(log max(v)) - O(1) along every branch; identify along which branches each extreme is approached. (iv) Attempt to sharpen the O(H) constant or exponent rigorously (e.g., exploit that the (1,1,c,d)-chain is the unique slowest branch and off-chain children grow by factor >= 4ab-1 with ab >= 2, so most of the tree grows much faster; try to prove N(H) = O(H^alpha) for some alpha < 1); if a sharper bound cannot be fully proved, state exactly what is proved, and label any improvement as CONJECTURE with the precise gap. KEEP COMPACT (well under 1200 words): theorems with terse proofs, explicit constants, no tables.
investigations.rationale: D4+D6 share one engine (multiplicative max-growth along tree edges); previous attempt died on output length, so the route is pre-digested and brevity is mandated. Conditional use of the tree structure is acceptable because struct-core-v2 proves it in the same wave and the two will be synthesized next.

investigations.acceptance_condition: Proved: the Vieta-root lemma (mutation preserves S); the (1,1,c_n,d_n) chain consists of solutions with exact closed form and growth 2+sqrt(3), giving N(H) >= log_{2+sqrt(3)} H - O(1); an honest branching-subtree attempt with distinctness and growth control proved, delivering the best rigorously provable bound with explicit constants; anything stronger labeled conjecture with the exact obstruction stated.

investigations.question: From first principles, prove the strongest rigorous lower bound for N(H). Compact plan: (A) The chain: define (c_0,d_0) = (1,3) and d_{n+1} = 4 d_n - c_n, c_{n+1} = d_n; prove by induction that (1,1,c_n,d_n) satisfies the equation (verify n=0: 1+1+1+9=12=4*3, and the induction step via the Vieta quadratic: if (1,1,c,d) is a solution then mutating c gives (1,1,d,4d-c), a solution by the Vieta root property - prove this root-swap lemma once) and that d_n strictly increases; solve the recurrence exactly (characteristic roots 2 +/- sqrt(3); compute the closed form for d_n correctly) and conclude N(H) >= log_{2+sqrt(3)}(H) - O(1), an explicit c*log(H) lower bound. (B) Power/super-log bound attack: at (1,1,c,d) with c >= 3 the child obtained by mutating a (=1) is (1,c,d,4cd-1) while mutating c gives (1,1,d,4d-c); prove these two children are distinct and that 4cd-1 <= 4*max^2; then consider the subtree generated by repeatedly taking either child, bound the depth reachable within max <= H (growth per edge <= 4*max^2 gives log-log type depth), and compute honestly what lower bound this delivers (e.g. N(H) >= c'(log H)^beta for the largest provable beta, or only c log H). Prove whichever is rigorously attainable with explicit constants; for anything stronger, state the precise obstruction as a labeled conjecture. All family members must be proved solutions (the Vieta-root lemma suffices) and proved distinct. KEEP COMPACT (well under 1200 words), no tables beyond 3 one-line checks.
investigations.rationale: D5 is independent of D4; constructive family arguments differ in character from tree counting. Previous attempt died on output length, so the recurrence and subtree strategy are pre-specified and brevity mandated.

investigations.question: D7+D9: Perform a BOUNDED, hand-checkable enumeration and report labeled observations only. Procedure (state it explicitly so it is reproducible by hand): (Method 1, direct search) enumerate all candidate solutions with d <= 100 by looping over sorted triples 1 <= a <= b <= c <= 100 and solving d^2 - (4abc) d + (a^2+b^2+c^2) = 0 for integer d >= c, using the cheap necessary condition d | a^2+b^2+c^2 to prune; (Method 2, BFS) list all vertices reachable from (1,1,1,1) by breadth-first mutation, mutating all 4 coordinates, re-sorting, discarding d > 100. Expected reachable set (verify each by direct substitution, one line each): (1,1,1,1), (1,1,1,3), (1,1,3,11), (1,1,11,41) - check whether anything else with d <= 100 appears (e.g. from (1,1,3,11), mutating a gives 131 > 100; from (1,1,11,41), mutating 11 gives 153 > 100, mutating 1 gives 1803 > 100). Report as LABELED OBSERVATIONS (enumeration bound d <= 100): (a) the complete verified table with one-line substitution checks; (b) whether any solution with c = d occurs; (c) whether any vertex has two distinct height-decreasing mutations / multiple parents (within the BFS check each vertex's parent is unique); (d) whether the two methods agree exactly (any direct-search solution not reachable from the root would locally refute D1); (e) descent sanity: for each non-root vertex compute d' = 4abc - d and confirm 1 <= d' < d, exhibiting the parent edge; (f) note any induction failure modes observed (e.g. re-sorting effects) or state their absence within the bound. STRICT BREVITY: total well under 900 words; distinguish verified facts within the bound from non-occurrences (which prove nothing beyond d <= 100).
investigations.rationale: D7 demands an active exception search before proof commitment and D9 demands labeled, reproducible enumeration; the bound d <= 100 keeps the hand work tiny (likely 4 vertices) while still cross-validating D1-D3 on all small cases and exercising every anomaly check.
